body.objective: Students will be able to write a design brief.
body.iCan: I can write a design brief.
successCriteria: I can write a design brief with purpose, user, criteria and constraints
I can plan a timeline and budget
I can sketch and choose a design solution
body.hook: A client says, "I want a website, and I want it to be amazing." That's not a plan. Designers turn vague wishes into a design brief: who it's for, what it must do, the budget, the deadline and the limits. Then the real work can start.

A limit on a project, such as budget, time, materials or size.
The planned amount of money for a project.
A schedule of tasks and deadlines.
An early model used to test an idea.
Repeating a cycle of designing, testing and improving.

study.title: Write the Brief
study.question: How do designers plan a project before building it?
study.passage:
Choose a project in your CTS area: a menu item for a café, a small piece of furniture, a garment, a brand logo, a mobile app screen, an electrical circuit project.
Part 1, Design brief (15 minutes): Write the brief with these headings:
• Problem or need: What needs solving?
• User: Who will use it?
• Requirements (criteria): What must it do? (3 to 5 measurable points)
• Constraints: budget, time, materials, size, safety rules
Part 2, Budget (10 minutes): List materials with quantity and unit cost; total them; add 10% contingency for mistakes.
Part 3, Timeline (10 minutes): List tasks in order, estimate hours for each and map them across class periods. Mark one checkpoint for a prototype.
Part 4, Ideation (15 minutes): Sketch three solutions. Score each against the requirements. Choose one and justify it.
Example budget line: pine board, 1 × 6 × 4 ft, 2 at $8.50 = $17.00.
study.source: Original design task written for this lesson.

Plan a timeline with a prototype checkpoint
